DEC-007.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): DNS-over-TLS (RFC 7858) transport. DoH (RFC 8484) is implemented but the TLS-over-853 DoT transport is missing, so the encrypted-DNS comparison story is incomplete. DoT is a first-class way to query a resolver over an encrypted, tamper-resistant channel and compare its answers against the system/custom/DoH paths side by side (the tool's signature 'compare resolvers to detect steering' capability). Add a repeatable --dot <host[:port]> flag + library dot_query reusing the in-tree rustls stack and the existing DNS wire builder/parser (build_query/parse_dns_response) so no new dependency is added (per DEC-002).
DEC-007.alternatives_rejected: HTTP response-body content capture (sensible next milestone but crosses all three HTTP protocol implementations, larger diff, and body content can be binary/sensitive); batch/multi-host diagnose sweep (new input+aggregation surface, larger scope); DoH-only enhancements (narrower, leaves the TLS transport gap)

ISS-001.summary: DoH (RFC 8484) is implemented, but the DNS-over-TLS transport (RFC 7858, TLS on port 853 with a 2-byte length prefix) is missing: a user cannot query a resolver over a TLS-protected DNS channel and compare it against the system/custom/DoH paths. A resolver or path that is tampered with or blocked at the UDP/plain-TCP level (e.g. an ISP that intercepts port 53) is invisible because there is no encrypted-DNS counterpart to compare other than DoH, and DoT is widely deployed (1.1.1.1:853, 8.8.8.8:853, dns.google).

TASK-001.summary: library dns::dot_query(endpoint, host, record_type, timeout, insecure): open a TCP connection to the resolver, drive a rustls TLS handshake with the endpoint hostname as SNI (port 853 default), send the hand-rolled DNS wire query with the 2-byte length prefix (RFC 7858 framing), read the length-prefixed response, and parse it with the existing parse_dns_response. Model gains ResolverKind::Dot(String). No new dependency (reuses in-tree rustls + existing wire builder/parser).

TASK-002.summary: dns --dot <host[:port]> repeatable flag (like --doh): thread through the dns subcommand single-shot and --count repeat paths, render ResolverKind::Dot rows in render_dns/render_dns_repeat, and document DoT alongside DoH in README. Fixture-gated integration test with an in-process TLS DoT server proving the query reaches it and the A record is parsed.

CHG-001.summary: dns --dot HOST[:PORT] adds DNS-over-TLS (RFC 7858): library dns::dot_query (raw DNS inside TLS on 853, reusing in-tree rustls + existing wire builder/parser, zero new deps), ResolverKind::Dot, CLI --dot threaded through single-shot and --count repeat, report renders DoT rows (human + JSON). parse_dot_endpoint unit test + dot_query doc-test + 2 fixture-gated integration tests (raw query returns canned A/AAAA; --count 3 aggregates 100%). 171 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.32%. commit 26926de

ISS-002.summary: dns --dot added the DNS-over-TLS transport, but diagnose still only folded --doh into its evidence/address pool, so a TLS-protected DNS comparison was unavailable in the full diagnostic pipeline (the diagnosis could not reason over DoT answers or probe DoT-resolved addresses).

TASK-003.summary: diagnose --dot <endpoint> (repeatable, like --doh): fold DNS-over-TLS answers into the full diagnostic pipeline's DNS evidence stack and probed address pool, so resolver-disagreement and steering detection can compare the local/--server path with a TLS-protected channel. Pinned by a fixture-gated test proving diagnose --dot surfaces the DoT-resolved record and renders the diagnosis.

CHG-002.summary: diagnose --dot <endpoint>: folds DoT answers into the diagnostic pipeline's DNS evidence + probed address pool (mirrors --doh). Fixture-gated test proves the DoT-resolved record appears in evidence and the diagnosis renders. 172 tests green, all gates clean. commit b0c5b89

DEC-008.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): HTTP response body content capture. The probes report status, headers and body size but discard the actual response body — yet the body is the decisive evidence for WHY an endpoint behaves as it does (a WAF block page, an auth/JSON error, a rate-limit message, a JS challenge, a captive-portal prompt). Capture a bounded, lossy-UTF8 textual snippet (first 1024 bytes) into HttpObservation and render it in the human report and JSON, completing the HTTP observation. The body is already read for sizing, so this costs no extra I/O and adds zero new dependencies; bounds and explicit truncation keep it safe on hostile/binary bodies.
DEC-008.alternatives_rejected: batch/multi-host diagnose sweep (new input+aggregation surface, larger scope); a --body opt-in CLI flag (extra CLI+API churn when always-bounded capture costs nothing — curl-like tools surface the body); probe --protocol dns (already rejected by DEC-006: dns repeat is hostname-centric)

ISS-003.summary: The HTTP probes (h1/h2/h3) count response body bytes but throw the content away, so a user cannot see WHAT an endpoint actually returned — the body is the decisive evidence for a WAF block page, an auth/JSON error, a rate-limit message, a JS challenge, or a captive-portal prompt, none of which a status code alone reveals.

TASK-004.summary: Capture a bounded lossy-UTF8 textual snippet of the HTTP response body (first 1024 bytes, explicit … truncation) into HttpObservation.body_snippet across http/http2/http3, using the body already read for sizing. CHG-003.summary: HttpObservation.body_snippet captures a bounded (1024-byte, lossy-UTF8, explicit …) textual snippet of the HTTP response body across h1/h2/h3 (reuses the body already read for sizing; zero new deps/flags); human report shows 'body content:' and --json carries it. Delivers a bounded full-body capture to a file, threading a body_output path through the shared probe fns + CLI (single-shot + repeat + diagnose) following the existing body/headers/path threading precedent (TASK-006/007). Public API change (regenerated api-baseline).
DEC-031.alternatives_rejected: raising the snippet cap (still truncates and balloons each report); no flag (forces re-run in curl); unbounded body streams (resource risk, keep 1 MiB cap); writing body in report layer (the library already drained it).

TASK-033.summary: Follow-on --output-body slice: thread the option through probe --protocol http|http2|http3 (repeat fns http_repeat_with_version/http2_repeat_with_version/http3_repeat via a body_output param) and diagnose's HTTP phases (collect_http_probes), so a repeated/sweep run can persist each response body too.

CHG-026.summary: Added --output-body FILE to single-shot http/http2/http3: body_output threaded through probe_impl and new *output public fns, full bounded body written verbatim best-effort; first slice (repeat/diagnose follow as TASK-033).

DEC-032.rationale: Reject the --output-body follow-on for the repeat probe and diagnose (supersedes TASK-033). The repeat probe aggregates N attempts into latency stats and diagnose runs HTTP/1.1+2+3 across every resolved address, so there is no single response body to persist — a single output file cannot represent N attempts or a 3-protocol multi-address sweep unambiguously (last-writer-wins would be misleading). The single-shot http/http2/http3 --output-body slice (CHG-026) already covers the full-body-inspection use case cleanly; repeat/diagnose remain latency/aggregate commands where a body dump has no clear meaning.
DEC-032.alternatives_rejected: writing only the last attempt/address body (arbitrary and confusing, not a real user need); lowering to a snippet-cap flag (out of scope, snippet already surfaced); requiring a directory of per-protocol files (scope creep, unclear naming)).

ISS-026.summary: The per-address probe commands (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe) resolve targets only via the system resolver and --server; --doh/--dot (encrypted-resolver resolution) are available on dns and diagnose but not on the probe commands, so an operator cannot probe through a tamper-resistant encrypted resolver even though diagnose already threads them through.

TASK-034.summary: Extend --doh/--dot to the per-address probe commands via resolve_for_tcp_servers: thread optional DoH/DoT endpoints (and the --insecure flag for their TLS) into resolution, query each for A+AAAA, and include the addresses so tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe can probe through an encrypted resolver like diagnose does.

DEC-033.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): --doh/--dot on the per-address probe commands. dns and diagnose already resolve through DNS-over-HTTPS/TLS; the probe commands (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe) only use system+--server. Threading the encrypted-resolver endpoints into the shared resolve_for_tcp_servers lets an operator probe through a tamper-resistant channel (steering detection parity with diagnose). No public API change (CLI + resolution only).
DEC-033.alternatives_rejected: only diagnosing through DoH/DoT (already exists, leaves the probe commands without it); a separate dns-into-atom subcommand (redundant with --server/--doh threading); making every probe open a DoH endpoint per address (not needed — resolve once per target).

CHG-027.summary: Extended --doh/--dot encrypted-resolver resolution to the per-address probe commands (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe): doh/dot endpoint lists + insecure threaded through resolve_for_tcp_servers and run_probe_flow; --doh/--dot added to every probe subcommand; no API change.

ISS-027.summary: The HTTP probes hard-code a 1 MiB MAX_BODY_BYTES read cap (and now --output-body writes only up to that cap), so an operator inspecting a >1 MiB response — a large API error, a big page, or a file download — cannot capture the full body; there is no way to raise or lower the cap at the CLI.

TASK-035.summary: Add --max-body-bytes N to http/http2/http3 (default 1 MiB) so the response-body read cap is configurable: thread a max_body_bytes param through probe_impl and the *output public fns, use it for both the read cap and the --output-body write, and keep the 1 KiB snippet semantics unchanged. Testable against the fixture's 2 MiB big.invalid route.

DEC-034.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): configurable --max-body-bytes on the HTTP-family probes. The probes hard-resource-bound body reads to 1 MiB (a deliberate safety cap) and --output-body inherits that limit, so a >1 MiB response cannot be captured. Making the cap configurable (default unchanged) lets an operator inspecting a large API error / big page / download raise the bound, while keeping the hostile-body safety valve intact. Threaded through the same probe_impl/CLI plumbing used by body/headers/output; snippet semantics unchanged. Public API change (regenerated api-baseline).
DEC-034.alternatives_rejected: raising the default cap (weakens the hostile-body resource bound for everyone); no flag (leaves >1 MiB bodies uncapturable); snippet-only (doesn't help --output-body).

CHG-028.summary: Added --max-body-bytes N to http/http2/http3: maxim_body_bytes threaded through probe_impl and the configurable *output entry points (now take max_body_bytes + optional output), driving both read cap and --output-body write; api-baseline regenerated; fixture test.

ISS-028.summary: The http/http2/http3 --csv output omits the negotiated TLS handshake details (version, cipher, ALPN, certificate subject/issuer/not_after) even though each HttpObservation already carries tls: Option<TlsObservation>, while tls --csv exposes them — so an HTTPS fleet sweep loaded into a spreadsheet loses the exact TLS evidence (protocol version, cipher, cert) that a TLS-only sweep gets.

TASK-036.summary: Extend render_http_csv (shared by http/http2/http3) to append TLS handshake columns (sni,version,cipher,alpn,subject,issuer,not_after_utc) sourced from each observation's embedded TlsObservation, mirroring tls --csv, so an HTTPS fleet sweep exposes the negotiated TLS evidence in CSV.

DEC-035.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface negotiated TLS handshake details in http/http2/http3 --csv. Each HttpObservation already embeds a TlsObservation, so the HTTP CSV can simply reuse it to expose version/cipher/ALPN/cert (matching tls --csv), closing a fleet-sweep observability gap without any new I/O or API change. No public API change (renderer-only).
DEC-035.alternatives_rejected: adding a separate http-tls subcommand (redundant with the embedded observation); duplicating the whole tls row set (kept to the same core handshake columns tls --csv uses); leaving it out (HTTPS sweeps lose cert/version evidence in spreadsheets).

CHG-029.summary: Extended http/http2/http3 --csv to expose negotiated TLS columns (sni,version,cipher,alpn,subject,issuer,not_after_utc) from the embedded TlsObservation, mirroring tls --csv; renderer-only, no API change; fixture test.

ISS-029.summary: The diagnose engine flags TLS handshake failures but has no automated verdict for an expiring or already-expired serving certificate — the TLS report annotates the remaining lifetime, yet a diagnose health sweep returns Healthy (or unrelated verdicts) instead of surfacing the expiring/expired cert, so an operator's automated monitoring misses a certificate that will break a service.

TASK-037.summary: Add an automated certificate-lifetime diagnosis: introduce DiagnosticCategory::Certificate, and a rule that scans TLS observations' certificates and raises a diagnosis when not_after is past (expired) or within 30 days (expiring), reusing the day-diff logic already used by the TLS report; render the new category and pin with unit tests (expired/expiring/far) plus api-baseline regeneration (public API change).

DEC-036.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): automated certificate-expiry diagnosis in the deterministic engine. The TLS report already annotates an expiring/expired cert, but diagnose returns Healthy or unrelated verdicts — so an automated health sweep cannot catch a cert that will break the service. Add DiagnosticCategory::Certificate + a certificate_lifetime_rules pass that reuses the report's day-diff (shared helper), raising an expired (Medium) or expiring-within-30-days (Low) verdict. Public API change (new category variant), regenerated api-baseline.
DEC-036.alternatives_rejected: leaving it to the human report (automated diagnose stays blind to cert expiry); over-engineering (per-cert chain inspection, revocation checks — out of scope and untestable); guessing a category name that implies path reachability (Certificate is distinct from Tls handshake).

CHG-030.summary: Added automated certificate-expiry diagnosis: DiagnosticCategory::Certificate + certificate_lifetime_rules (Medium expired / Low expiring within 30d) reusing the report's shared day-diff helpers; api-baseline regenerated; unit tests.

ISS-030.summary: The TLS report shows a covers <sni>: no verdict when the served certificate's SANs do not cover the presented hostname, but the diagnose engine raises no automated verdict for a wrong-host or wildcard-mismatch certificate — so a scripted/CI diagnose sweep under --insecure (where chain validation is skipped and the mismatch is otherwise silent) misses a cert that is not valid for the host being served.

TASK-038.summary: Add an automated certificate hostname-coverage diagnosis: share cert_covers_hostname as pub(crate), add a rule that scans TLS observations and raises a Certificate diagnosis (Medium) when the cert's SANs do not cover observation.sni (wrong-host / wildcard mismatch), reusing the report matcher so report and engine agree. Pin with unit tests for exact/wildcard/IP/coverage cases; no new category needed (reuses Certificate).

DEC-037.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): automate certificate hostname-coverage diagnosis. The report already surfaces covers <sni>: no, but diagnose stays silent, so a CI health sweep under --insecure misses a wrong-host/wildcard-mismatch cert. Add a rule sharing the report's cert_covers_hostname matcher (pub(crate)) and raising a Medium Certificate diagnosis when the SANs don't cover the presented SNI. Reuses the Certificate category from DEC-036; no new API change (matcher made pub(crate) only).
DEC-037.alternatives_rejected: a new category (reuses Certificate, cleaner); duplicating the matcher in diagnostics (drift risk); only matching IP literals (DNS wildcard/exact mismatch also matters); raising High (a coverage mismatch alone is Medium; chain validation would fail loudly without --insecure).

CHG-031.summary: Added certificate_coverage_rules: Medium Certificate diagnosis on SAN/SNI mismatch, empty SANs, or wrong-apex wildcard, sharing cert_covers_hostname (pub(crate)); no new public API; unit tests.

ISS-031.summary: The single-shot http/http2/http3 probes accept --max-body-bytes, but diagnose — which runs the exact same library probes in its HTTP phase — cannot bound its response-body reads, so a diagnose run always uses the fixed 1 MiB default and cannot observe a larger body (e.g. a big API page) in its HTTP evidence.

TASK-039.summary: Thread diagnose --max-body-bytes through the HTTP phase: parse the flag, route the http/http2/http3 probe calls in collect_http_probes through the configurable *_output entry points (passing max_body_bytes and None output), so a diagnose run can raise/lower the response-body read cap like the single-shot probes. No output-body (rejected DEC-032); scalar cap only. Pinned by a fixture-gated test on big.invalid.

DEC-038.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): diagnose --max-body-bytes. The HTTP phase of diagnose runs the same http/http2/http3 probes that now carry a configurable body cap, but diagnose hard-codes the 1 MiB default. Thread the flag through collect_http_probes (via the *_output variants with None output), so a diagnose run can bound >1 MiB response reads — parity with the single-shot probes. This is distinct from the rejected DEC-032 output-body on diagnose (a scalar read bound has an unambiguous meaning; writing a body does not). No public API change (CLI + internal threading).
DEC-038.alternatives_rejected: adding --output-body to diagnose (rejected DEC-032 as ambiguous across protocols/addresses); leaving it fixed at 1 MiB (diagnose cannot observe large bodies); only easing on tls phase (unrelated).

CHG-032.summary: Threaded diagnose --max-body-bytes through the HTTP phase via the configurable probe entry points (scalar cap, None output); no API change; fixture test.

ISS-032.summary: The tls command's human report shows a cert : row and a covers <sni>: yes/no verdict, but the http/http2/http3 human report shows only TLS/ALPN — it drops the certificate and the SAN-coverage verdict even though every HTTPS observation carries the full TlsObservation. An operator inspecting HTTPS (or probing with --insecure, where coverage is the only mismatch signal) loses the wrong-host/wildcard verdict in the terminal.

TASK-040.summary: Surface the certificate row (cert :) and the covers <sni>: yes/no verdict in the http/http2/http3 human report, sourced from each observation's embedded TlsObservation via the shared render_cert/cert_covers_hostname — parity with the tls command. Renderer-only, no public API change. Pinned by report unit + fixture tests.

DEC-039.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface cert + coverage verdict in the http/http2/http3 human report. The tls command already shows cert : and covers <sni>: yes/no; the HTTPS report drops them (only TLS/ALPN), so an operator inspecting HTTPS — especially under --insecure where coverage is the only mismatch signal — cannot see the wrong-host/wildcard verdict in the terminal. Reuse shared render_cert/cert_covers_hostname; renderer-only, no API change. Complements the automated diagnose coverage rule (DEC-037).
DEC-039.alternatives_rejected: relying on the automated diagnose rule (doesn't help plain http output inspection); duplicating a richer cert block (keep parity with tls: one cert row + covers line); leaving it out (HTTPS inspection stays blind to coverage verdict).

CHG-033.summary: HTTP human report now shows cert row + covers verdict via shared render_cert/cert_covers_hostname; renderer-only, no API change; unit + fixture tests.

ISS-033.summary: The dns subcommand runs its multi-target DNS health sweep strictly sequentially (for target in targets { dns_compute }), so a sweep across many hosts/resolvers is serialized by the slowest resolver — while the per-address probe commands (tcp/tls/http/...) already bound their fleet sweeps with --concurrency. There is no way to parallelize a DNS health sweep.

TASK-041.summary: Add dns --concurrency N (default 1, keeping current sequential behavior) to parallelize the multi-target DNS health sweep via the shared parallel_map helper, then re-sort outputs back to input-target order so human/JSON/CSV rendering stays deterministic. Pinned by a CLI test that multi-target dns still works with --concurrency and clamps invalid values.

DEC-040.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): dns --concurrency to parallelize multi-target DNS health sweeps. dns runs targets sequentially while the probe commands already bound fleet sweeps with --concurrency, so a large DNS sweep is serialized by the slowest resolver. Add --concurrency (default 1 preserves today's exact output order and semantics) via the shared parallel_map helper, re-sorting outputs by input order so rendering stays deterministic. No public API change.
DEC-040.alternatives_rejected: always-parallel (changes default output/semantics); no flag (leaves DNS sweeps serialized); parallelizing resolvers within a single host before targets (bigger, address-target parallel is the sweep-level win).

CHG-034.summary: Added dns --concurrency N (default 1) to parallelize multi-target DNS health sweeps via parallel_map, re-sorting outputs to input order; no API change; CLI test.

ISS-034.summary: The diagnostic engine flags HTTP status >= 400 and stalled bodies, but is silent on a 3xx redirect — even though a redirect is a very common real-world observation (a captive portal, a login/auth wall, a moved domain, or middleware rewriting). diagnose currently returns Healthy (or unrelated verdicts) for a host that redirects, so an automated health sweep cannot tell you 'this host redirected to X'.

TASK-042.summary: Add an automated redirect diagnosis: a rule that scans HTTP observations and, when a 3xx status with a Location is observed on an otherwise-reachable host, raises a Low Http diagnosis naming the redirect target — surfacing captive-portal / login-wall / moved-domain evidence that today is invisible to diagnose. Pinned by a unit test and a fixture-gated test using the redirect.invalid 302 route; no new category needed (reuses Http).

DEC-041.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): automate redirect observation into a diagnosis. The engine flags >=400 and stalled bodies but is silent on 3xx redirects — yet a host that redirects you (captive portal, auth wall, moved domain, middleware rewrite) is a very common real-world observable. Add a redirect rule that raises a Low Http diagnosis naming the Location when a 3xx status occurs on a reachable host, reusing the Http category. No new public API (rule only). Complements the existing Dec-003 'redirect is an observation' stance — this surfaces it in diagnose, not by following it.
DEC-041.alternatives_rejected: a new category (reuses Http, cleaner); following redirects (explicitly rejected DEC-003); raising Medium (a redirect is not inherently a failure — Low); only 4xx/redirect-to-login heuristic (capturing any 3xx + Location is the honest, simple signal).

CHG-035.summary: Added an automated redirect diagnosis: redirect_rules scans HTTP observations and raises a Low Http diagnosis naming the Location when a 3xx status occurs on a reachable host. Wired into the diagnose dispatch, unit-tested (fires on 3xx+Location, silent on 2xx/failure) and fixture-gated via diagnose --sni redirect.invalid.

ISS-035.summary: The diagnostic engine checks certificate expiry (notAfter in the past / near-expiry) but is silent on a certificate that is NOT YET valid — a notBefore in the future. Under --insecure, chain validation is skipped, so a host presenting a premature cert reports Healthy while real clients (and any validation path) would refuse it. not_before_utc is already captured on the CertificateSummary but never analyzed.

TASK-043.summary: Add a not-yet-valid certificate diagnosis to the lifetime rule family: when a peer cert's notBefore is in the future (days_until > 0), raise a Medium Certificate diagnosis naming how far in the future validity starts, with clock-skew / premature-issuance causes. Pinned by a unit test building a future notBefore.

DEC-042.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): flag not-yet-valid certificates. The lifetime rules handle expired and near-expiry but ignore a future notBefore — under --insecure that yields a false Healthy for a host whose cert is not yet valid. Add a Medium Certificate verdict when notBefore is in the future, reusing the existing report days_until helper and the Certificate category (no API change, rule only). Mirrors the accepted expiry/coverage series (DEC-036/037).
DEC-042.alternatives_rejected: a new category (reuses Certificate); raising High confidence (future notBefore is inherently ambiguous — client or server clock skew — so Medium); a separate rule file (belongs in the lifetime family); flagging same-day notBefore (integer-day granularity: only strictly-future dates, avoiding clock jitter)

CHG-036.summary: Added a not-yet-valid certificate rule to the lifetime family: when a peer cert's notBefore is in the future (integer-day days_until > 0), raise a Medium Certificate diagnosis naming how far off validity starts, with misissuance / clock-skew / premature-deployment causes. Unit-tested (future notBefore raises; past notBefore silent).

ISS-036.summary: diagnose runs a multi-target fleet sweep sequentially (for target in targets), so with N hosts each waits for the previous host's full pipeline. dns already gained --concurrency for its multi-target sweep (DEC-040) but diagnose never did -- a large health sweep is needlessly slow and does not scale.

TASK-044.summary: Parallelize diagnose across targets: run the per-host pipeline concurrently bounded by the existing --concurrency flag (1 = strictly sequential), re-sorting reports back to the given target order so human/JSON/CSV output stays deterministic. Reuses parallel_map + index re-sort exactly like dns --concurrency (DEC-040). Pinned by a fixture test asserting input order is preserved under --concurrency 4.

DEC-043.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): make diagnose's fleet sweep scale by sweeping hosts concurrently. dns already gained --concurrency for its multi-target sweep (DEC-040) and the operator values it; diagnose is the fleet/health command so it should too. Reuse the existing --concurrency flag (also bounds per-host address probes), re-sort reports by input index so output stays deterministic, and keep --concurrency 1 as the strictly-sequential baseline. No API/format change.
DEC-043.alternatives_rejected: a separate flag (--concurrency already exists and reads naturally as a global probe bound); changing output order (no — index re-sort preserves it); touching the probe subcommands (out of scope; they already use concurrency for addresses)

CHG-037.summary: Parallelized the diagnose multi-target sweep: the per-host pipeline now runs concurrently bounded by --concurrency (1 stays strictly sequential), using parallel_map + index re-sort so human/JSON/CSV output stays in input order (mirrors dns --concurrency, DEC-040). Updated --concurrency docs in README; pinned by a fixture test asserting input order is preserved under --concurrency 4.

ISS-037.summary: The per-address probe subcommands (tcp, tls, http, http2, http3, probe) share run_probe_flow, which sweeps a fleet of targets sequentially per host — each target waits for the previous. diagnose already gained concurrent sweeps (TASK-044) but these connectivity sweeps did not, so large fleet probes are needlessly slow.

TASK-045.summary: Parallelize the shared probe sweep (run_probe_flow, used by tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe) across targets: run the per-host resolve+probe concurrently bounded by --concurrency (1 = strictly sequential), re-sorting per-target results back to input order so human/JSON/CSV output stays deterministic. Mirrors diagnose TASK-044 and dns DEC-040. Pinned by a fixture test asserting a tcp sweep preserves input order under --concurrency 4.

DEC-044.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): extend the accepted concurrent-sweep direction (dns DEC-040, diagnose TASK-044) to the per-address probe subcommands. They share run_probe_flow, so parallelizing there fixes all of tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe at once. Reuse --concurrency (also bounds per-address probes), re-sort by input index so output stays deterministic, keep --concurrency 1 as the sequential baseline. No API/format change.
DEC-044.alternatives_rejected: a per-subcommand flag (they share run_probe_flow; reusing --concurrency is consistent); changing output order (no — index re-sort preserves it); leaving diagnose-only (inconsistent — probe sweeps are the same user story).

CHG-038.summary: Parallelized the shared probe sweep (run_probe_flow) across targets: tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe now resolve+probe hosts concurrently bounded by --concurrency (1 stays strictly sequential), re-sorting per-target results back to input order so human/JSON/CSV output stays deterministic (mirrors diagnose TASK-044 and dns DEC-040). Updated the fleet-sweep README; pinned by a fixture test asserting a tcp sweep preserves input order under --concurrency 4.

ISS-038.summary: The repo maintains a detailed Keep-a-Changelog Unreleased/Added section documenting every feature with its test evidence, but the four most recent milestones did not add entries: redirect diagnosis (CHG-035), not-yet-valid certificate (CHG-036), diagnose concurrent sweep (CHG-037) and probe concurrent sweep (CHG-038). The CHANGELOG is a documented deliverable; omitting these features breaks the acceptance convention and makes the release notes incomplete.

TASK-046.summary: Add Keep-a-Changelog entries for the four most recent milestones (redirect diagnosis, not-yet-valid certificate, diagnose concurrent sweep, probe concurrent sweep), each in the repo's established style (user-visible behaviour + public-API note + pinned-by-test evidence), inserted at the top of Unreleased/Added (newest-first), verified lint-clean under rumdl.

DEC-045.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): close the changelog acceptance gap. The four most recent milestones shipped without CHANGELOG entries, violating the repo's documented Keep-a-Changelog convention (every prior feature has an entry with test evidence). Add the four entries in the established style so the Unreleased notes are complete and accurate. Catches a real gap in delivery acceptance, not a cosmetic nicety.
DEC-045.alternatives_rejected: regenerating/auto-filling the whole changelog (out of scope, and the convention is hand-maintained); deferring until release (the Unreleased section should track each feature as it lands); editing entries for prior milestones (they are already correctly documented).

CHG-039.summary: Added four Keep-a-Changelog Unreleased/Added entries (newest-first at the top) documenting the redirect diagnosis, not-yet-valid certificate, diagnose concurrent sweep and probe concurrent sweep milestones, each in the repo's established style with a public-API note and pinned-by-test evidence. Verified no new rumdl lint issues from the additions.

ISS-039.summary: The DNS diagnostics support A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT/NS/SOA/CAA/SRV but have no PTR/reverse-DNS query, so an operator cannot answer the common 'what hostname is behind this IP' question (rDNS for mail/anti-spam, identifying infrastructure, CDN reconciliation) with dns. Reverse lookups require constructing the reverse-zone name (in-addr.arpa / ip6.arpa), which is tedious to do by hand.

TASK-047.summary: Add PTR (reverse DNS) support: DnsRecordType::Ptr + DnsRecord::Ptr, wire the PTR lookup through the hickory resolver path, the DoH/DoT wire builder+parser (type 12), and parse_record_type; when the target is an IP literal, auto-construct the reverse-zone name (in-addr.arpa / ip6.arpa) so  just works and reports the user's literal target. Pinned by unit tests for the wire/name/reverse-zone helpers and a fixture CLI test against a canned PTR responder.

DEC-046.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): add reverse DNS (PTR). The dns surface covers every forward record type but no PTR, so rDNS (mail anti-spam verification, identifying the hostname behind an IP, CDN/infra reconciliation) is not possible. PTR is a single-name rdata like CNAME/NS, so it slots cleanly into the existing typed-record, hickory, and wire builder/parser pipeline. Auto-construct the reverse-zone name from an IP target so the common 'dns --record-type PTR <ip>' command reads naturally. Public API change (two new enum variants); api-baseline regenerated.
DEC-046.alternatives_rejected: a separate reverse/ptr subcommand (--record-type PTR is the natural, minimal surface); requiring the user to pass the arpa name manually (poor UX; auto-construction is deterministic and standard); treating PTR as non-diagnostic (reverse DNS is a normal dns capability).

CHG-040.summary: Added PTR (reverse DNS) support: DnsRecordType::Ptr + DnsRecord::Ptr, hickory lookup mapping, DoH/DoT wire builder+parser type 12, parse_record_type PTR, and auto reverse-zone construction (in-addr.arpa / ip6.arpa) so 'dns --record-type PTR <ip>' resolves the mapped hostname(s). Report rt_label/order extended; api-baseline regenerated; README + CHANGELOG updated. Pinned by unit tests (reverse_zone v4/v6, qtype 12, wire PTR decode, parse_record_type) and a fixture CLI test surfacing host.example via --doh /dns-ptr-query.

ISS-040.summary: The diagnostic engine reports per-layer failures (HTTP >=400, truncated bodies, redirects, QUIC failures) but never looks ACROSS paths: a host that returns a different response class over one wire protocol than another on the same destination (e.g. HTTP/1.1 -> 200 but HTTP/2 -> 403), or over one address family than the other (IPv4 200 vs IPv6 503), is a real split-brain signal — a CDN edge / WAF treating protocols or families differently, an A/B or partial deployment, or a per-family cloud edge — yet diagnose reports it Healthy because every path technically works.

TASK-048.summary: Add a cross-path HTTP consistency rule to the engine: compare only completed HTTP responses (status present, no failure) and raise a Low Http diagnosis when (a) the same destination returns a 2xx on one wire protocol and a non-2xx on another, or (b) one address family is uniformly 2xx while the other returns any non-2xx. Proton/negotiation failures and stalls stay owned by their own layer rules. Confidence Medium, evidence names the per-path statuses; conservative to avoid false positives. Pinned by unit tests for each sub-signal and quiet healthy/negotiation-failure cases.

DEC-047.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface cross-path HTTP inconsistency. The engine aggregates per-layer failures but never compares response classes across protocols or address families, so a host whose paths disagree (CDN edge / WAF split-ACL, A/B deployment, per-family cloud edge) can report Healthy. Compare only completed responses (status present, no failure) so protocol-negotiation failures and stalls stay owned by their own rules; bucket by 2xx-vs-non-2xx to avoid benign status-detail noise; Low severity + Medium confidence with honest alternatives. Reuses the Http category; no new dependency or API.
DEC-047.alternatives_rejected: a new category (reuses Http); flagging exact-status != (too noisy: 200 vs 204 vs 302); comparing failed/timed-out observations as a consistency signal (that is other rules' job, and would double count); High severity (a divergent path is not an outage — the host still serves); based on thresholds (none needed — it is a factual status comparison).

CHG-041.summary: Added http_consistency_rules to the diagnostic engine: raises a Low Http diagnosis (Medium confidence) when completed responses diverge across wire protocols on the same destination (2xx on one, non-2xx on another) or across address families (one family all-2xx, the other any non-2xx). Only completed responses (status present, no failure) are compared and bucketed 2xx-vs-non-2xx so negotiation failures/stalls stay owned by their own rules and benign status-detail differences are ignored. Wired into diagnose dispatch; CHANGELOG updated. Pinned by unit tests for cross-protocol, cross-family, and quiet healthy/negotiation-failure/single-protocol cases.

ISS-041.summary: dns --record-type PTR <ip> silently ignores --count N: the reverse-lookup branch always returns a single-shot observation, unlike every other record type which --count aggregates into per-resolver latency/failure stats. A user repeating a reverse lookup to gauge stability would get misleading single-shot output with a silently-dropped flag.

TASK-049.summary: Make dns --count work for PTR reverse lookups: when the target is an IP literal and --count > 1, route the PTR query on the auto-built reverse-zone name through the existing resolve_repeat + encrypted_repeat aggregation (reporting the user's IP as the report host), so reverse-lookup stability is aggregated exactly like every other record type. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: dns --record-type PTR 192.0.2.77 --doh ... --count 3 renders a 3/3 repeat row.

DEC-048.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): complete PTR --count parity. The PTR milestone (DEC-046) shipped single-shot reverse lookups but silently ignored --count, diverging from every forward record type that aggregates repeats. Route IP-literal PTR repeats through the existing resolve_repeat/encrypted_repeat path on the reverse-zone name, keeping TargetDns.host as the user's IP. Small, robust, no new dependency; reuses the exact aggregation every other type uses.
DEC-048.alternatives_rejected: clamping/rejecting --count on PTR (worse DX — the flag should just work, and the aggregation is already generic); a manual repeat loop (already provided by resolve_repeat/encrypted_repeat); keeping the silent ignore (a documented-elsewhere silently dropped flag is a correctness bug).

CHG-042.summary: Made dns --count work for PTR reverse lookups: an IP-literal PTR target with --count > 1 now routes the reverse-zone query through the existing resolve_repeat + encrypted_repeat aggregation (reporting the user's IP as the report host) instead of silently ignoring the count. Updated the PTR CHANGELOG entry. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test asserting --count 3 renders a 3/3 repeat row labeled with the target IP.

ISS-042.summary: diagnose probes forward DNS (A/AAAA) but never reverse DNS, so when an operator diagnoses an IP literal they cannot see the hostname rDNS maps to it (identifying what server/infrastructure they are actually probing). dns --record-type PTR exists (TASK-047) but the flagship 'full picture' diagnose command omits it, leaving an identification gap for IP-targeted diagnostics.

TASK-050.summary: Add an opt-in --reverse flag to diagnose: for an IP-literal target, build the reverse-zone name (reusing the shared reverse_zone helper) and add a PTR DnsObservation to the DNS evidence stack (system + --server + --doh + --dot resolvers), so the identify-the-host rDNS name surfaces in human/JSON output. Evidence-only (no diagnosis, since many IPs legitimately lack PTR), so --strict is unaffected. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: diagnose 192.0.2.77 --reverse --doh <fixture>/dns-ptr-query --insecure surfaces host.example.

DEC-049.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): add reverse DNS context to diagnose for IP-literal targets. dns got PTR (DEC-046) but diagnose -- the flagship full-picture command -- still cannot show what hostname rDNS maps an IP to, which is how an operator identifies what they are probing. Add an opt-in --reverse flag (keeps default diagnose behavior unchanged), reusing the shared reverse_zone helper and the same PTR query path. Evidence-only, so absent PTR is never an anomaly and --strict is unaffected. No new dependency or API.
DEC-049.alternatives_rejected: always-on reverse for every target (adds a query+noise to every run; opt-in is right); hostname targets reverse-resolving every resolved IP (complex and noisy; IP-literal is the clean, unambiguous use); folding into an existing flag (a dedicated --reverse reads clearly).

CHG-043.summary: Added diagnose --reverse: for an IP-literal target, builds the reverse-zone name via the now-shared reverse_zone helper and queries PTR through system/--server + --doh/--dot resolvers, adding the mapped hostname to the DNS evidence stack (human + JSON). Opt-in and evidence-only (absent PTR never raises an anomaly; --strict unaffected). Shared reverse_zone exposed pub(super); --reverse arg added to the diagnose command. README + CHANGELOG updated. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: diagnose 192.0.2.77 --reverse --doh /dns-ptr-query surfaces host.example.

ISS-043.summary: diagnose --reverse was only implemented for IP-literal targets, so diagnosing a hostname with --reverse silently did nothing -- the same class of silently-ignored flag previously fixed for PTR --count (ISS-041). A user expecting reverse-DNS context for a hostname got none, without any indication.

TASK-051.summary: Extend diagnose --reverse to hostname targets: reverse-resolve each resolved address (in addition to the IP-literal case) and label each PTR evidence row with the reversed IP, so the flag is never silently ignored. Reuses the shared reverse_zone helper and PTR query path. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: diagnose host.example --reverse with the fixture's /dns-query + /dns-ptr-query surfaces the PTR evidence.

DEC-050.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): complete diagnose --reverse parity. DEC-049 shipped --reverse only for IP-literal targets, so hostname targets silently ignored it -- a flag consistency bug matching the PTR --count fix (ISS-041). Extend --reverse to reverse each resolved address of a hostname target, labeling PTR rows with the reversed IP (clear, consistent, never silent). Reuses the shared reverse_zone helper and PTR query path; no new dependency or API.
DEC-050.alternatives_rejected: warning/erroring on hostname --reverse (worse DX and noisy in a sweep; the flag should just work); keeping the silent ignore (a silently dropped flag is a correctness bug); a separate flag for hostname reverse (unneeded -- one --reverse covers both).

CHG-044.summary: Extended diagnose --reverse to hostname targets: it now reverse-resolves each resolved address (in addition to the IP-literal case) and labels each PTR evidence row with the reversed IP, so the flag is never silently ignored. Reuses the shared reverse_zone helper + PTR query path; CHANGELOG updated. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: diagnose host.example --reverse with the fixture's /dns-query + /dns-ptr-query surfaces the PTR evidence.

ISS-044.summary: probe --protocol http|http2|http3 repeats an HTTP endpoint for stability but surfaces no HTTP status codes: the aggregate treats any completed response (including 4xx/5xx) as transport success, so a host returning 503 on every attempt shows 100% success and the operator cannot see status flapping (e.g. 200x8 vs 503x2) that is exactly what a repeat probe exists to reveal.

TASK-052.summary: Surface the HTTP status distribution in the repeat probes: carry each attempt's status through the shared repeat_impl aggregation, add a status_counts histogram (StatusCount struct) to ProbeResult, and render it in the probe human report and JSON. Keep the documented transport-success semantics (a completed response with any status counts as a successful exchange) — the addition is visibility, not a semantics change. Public API change (ProbeResult gains status_counts; api-baseline regenerated). Pinned by an aggregation unit test and a fixture-gated CLI test: probe --protocol http --count N shows the observed statuses.

DEC-051.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface HTTP statuses in the repeat probes. http_outcome deliberately counts a completed response (even 5xx) as transport success -- a defensible connectivity-first design -- but the probe report relays zero status information, so repeat-probing an HTTP endpoint cannot reveal status flapping (200x8 vs 503x2), which is the whole point of a stability probe. Add a status_counts histogram to ProbeResult, threaded through the shared repeat_impl, without changing the documented success semantics; render it in human + JSON. Public API change (regenerate api-baseline).
DEC-051.alternatives_rejected: redefining 5xx as failure (contradicts the deliberate transport-success semantics and would break --strict meaning); a separate probe subcommand flag that only prints status (the histogram belongs in the existing repeat report); changing http_outcome success (same reason as redefining 5xx).

CHG-045.summary: Added an HTTP status distribution to the repeat probes: repeat_impl now carries each attempt's status and aggregates a status_counts histogram (new StatusCount model + ProbeResult.status_counts), rendered in the probe human report (status: 200xN, ...) and JSON, so repeat-probing an HTTP endpoint reveals status flapping that transport pass/fail counts hide. Transport-success semantics preserved (a completed response with any status still counts as a successful exchange). Public API change (api-baseline regenerated); tcp/tls repeats keep an empty list. Pinned by an aggregation unit test and a fixture-gated CLI test surfacing 200x3.

ISS-045.summary: probe --protocol http now surfaces the HTTP status distribution in human and JSON output (TASK-052), but the probe --csv exporter still emits only host,destination,attempts,success_rate,latency...failures -- the statuses added to the feature are missing from the CSV path, so a spreadsheet repeat-probe load cannot see statuses, an inconsistency within the delivered feature.

TASK-053.summary: Add a statuses column to probe --csv: emit the ProbeResult.status_counts distribution (e.g. 200x3;503x2) per destination row, empty for the tcp/tls transport repeats, so the CSV path is consistent with the human/JSON output of the status feature. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: probe --protocol http --count 3 --csv carries 200x3, and the existing tcp --csv header/rows were updated to include the column.

DEC-052.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): complete the probe status feature across output formats. TASK-052 delivered the status distribution to human + JSON but not the probe --csv exporter, leaving an inconsistency (a spreadsheet repeat-probe load cannot see statuses). Add a statuses column to render_probe_csv (empty for tcp/tls repeats, '200x3;503x2' semicolon-joined for HTTP), keeping the RFC-4180 quoting convention. No public API change (renderer only).
DEC-052.alternatives_rejected: leaving CSV without statuses (the feature is inconsistent across formats); a separate --csv flag just for statuses (one column belongs in the existing exporter); piping statuses through a fragile multi-row format (a single semicolon-joined column is clean and CSV-safe).

CHG-046.summary: Added a statuses column to probe --csv: render_probe_csv now emits the ProbeResult.status_counts distribution (e.g. 200x3;503x2, semicolon-joined, RFC-4180 quoted) per destination row, empty for the tcp/tls transport repeats, matching the human/JSON output of the status feature. Updated the CSV test's expected header and added a fixture-gated CLI test (probe --protocol http --count 3 --csv carries 200x3). Renderer-only, no public API change; CHANGELOG updated.

ISS-046.summary: Every multi-target fleet command (dns, tcp, tls, http, http2, http3, probe, diagnose) requires the target list inline on the shell command line, even though the CLI already supports reading --header and --body from a file or stdin (@path / -). A large fleet sweep targets dozens/hundreds of hosts, where an inline command line is impractical and error-prone; the target-list path is inconsistent with the existing @file/- convention.

TASK-054.summary: Let every multi-target fleet command read its target list from a file or stdin: add a shared parse_targets helper in the cli that, for each positional target, expands @path to the file's lines (skipping blanks and # comments) and - to stdin lines, then parses each as host[:port] (parity with --header/--body). Replace the three duplicated inline target loops with it, so dns/tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose all support it. No public API change. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: dns @file and dns - (stdin) each resolve 1.1.1.1 + 8.8.8.8.

DEC-053.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): add target lists from file/stdin to the fleet sweeps. The CLI already reads --header/--body from @file or - (stdin), but a sweep's target list still had to be inline, which is impractical for dozens/hundreds of hosts. Centralize target parsing in a shared parse_targets helper (expanding @path to lines, - to stdin, parity with --header/--body) and replace the three duplicated loops, so every multi-target command gains it consistently. No public API change.
DEC-053.alternatives_rejected: only diagnose/dns (inconsistent -- the loop is shared and every sweep deserves it); a separate --targets flag (a positional @path/- is the established convention); keeping inline-only (ignores a real fleet-ops need and an existing CLI convention).

CHG-047.summary: Added target-list-from-file/stdin support to every multi-target fleet command via a shared parse_targets helper in the cli (each positional target expands @path to the file lines, skipping blanks and # comments, and - to stdin lines), replacing the three duplicated inline target loops in run_probe_flow/diagnose/dns. No public API change; README + CHANGELOG updated. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: dns @file and dns - (stdin) each resolve 1.1.1.1 + 8.8.8.8.

ISS-047.summary: The dns diagnostic does not report record time-to-live (TTL) anywhere: hickory answers (which carry TTL) are reduced to DnsRecord values and the DoH/DoT wire parser skips the TTL field. TTL is a standard, useful DNS data point (cache duration, propagation timing, diagnosing stale/shadowing records) that dig reports by default, so the tool's DNS output is missing a core field.

TASK-055.summary: Surface DNS record TTL: add a ttl field to DnsObservation, populate it from the hickory system/--server lookup (first matching answer's TTL) and from the DoH/DoT wire parser (the answer TTL already in the message), and render it in the dns human report and JSON. No new dependency. Public API change (DnsObservation gains ttl; api-baseline regenerated). Pinned by a wire-parser TTL unit test and a fixture-gated CLI test asserting the fixture DoH answer's TTL renders.

DEC-054.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface DNS TTL. The tool reports every record type but not TTL -- the caching/propagation datum dig shows by default -- so DNS output is missing a core field. Capture it from the hickory lookup answers and from the DoH/DoT wire parser (the 4-byte TTL is already in each answer), store it on DnsObservation, and render it. No new dependency. Public API change (regenerate api-baseline).
DEC-054.alternatives_rejected: per-record DnsRecord variants carrying TTL (changes every variant; a per-observation TTL from the first answer is simpler and matches how a single A/AAAA lookup reports); a TTL-multiplication helper (not the tool's job); leaving TTL out (a standard DNS field a diagnostics tool should report).

CHG-048.summary: Added DNS record TTL to dns output: DnsObservation gains a ttl: Option<u32> field, populated from the hickory system/--server lookup (first matching answer's ttl) and from the DoH/DoT wire parser (the first answer's TTL, which the parser previously skipped). Render_dns shows '..., ttl Ns' and --json carries it. Public API change (api-baseline regenerated); no new dependency. Pinned by a wire-parser TTL unit test and the DoH fixture CLI test asserting the canned 60s TTL renders.

ISS-048.summary: The DNS TTL milestone (TASK-055) surfaced the record time-to-live in the dns report and --json, but the dns --csv exporter still emits only host,resolver,record_type,attempts,success_rate,latency_p50_ms,latency_p95_ms,latency_max_ms,failures -- the spreadsheet export loses TTL, the same format-parity gap the probe status feature closed (ISS-045).

TASK-056.summary: Add a ttl column to dns --csv: emit the DnsObservation.ttl (single-shot rows; repeat --count rows aggregate away per-answer TTL so the field stays empty), so the spreadsheet export is consistent with the human/JSON TTL feature. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: dns host.example --doh <fixture>/dns-query --insecure --csv carries the 60s TTL.

DEC-055.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): complete DNS TTL across output formats. TASK-055 delivered TTL to human + JSON but not the dns --csv exporter, leaving an inconsistency (a spreadsheet health sweep cannot see the caching/propagation datum) -- the same parity gap the probe status feature closed (DEC-052/DEC-053).
DEC-055.alternatives_rejected: leaving dns --csv without a ttl column (the exporters would disagree on the same feature); piping TTL through the --count repeat aggregation (repeat rows intentionally aggregate away per-answer TTL, mirroring how the human repeat report omits it); a separate --csv flag just for TTL (one column belongs in the existing exporter).

CHG-049.summary: Added a ttl column to dns --csv: render_dns_csv now emits host,resolver,record_type,attempts,success_rate,latency_p50_ms,latency_p95_ms,latency_max_ms,failures,ttl, populating the field from DnsObservation.ttl on single-shot rows and leaving it empty for --count repeat rows (which aggregate away the per-answer TTL), so the spreadsheet export matches the human/JSON TTL feature.

ISS-049.summary: The response-header feature (observed headers bounded to 24) surfaces in the human http/http2/http3 report and --json, but the single-shot --csv exporter (render_http_csv) still emits only host,destination,protocol,status,location,body_bytes,ttfb_ms,latency_ms,sni,version,cipher,alpn,subject,issuer,not_after_utc,failure -- a spreadsheet fleet sweep loses the server/edge/caching evidence that human and JSON show.

TASK-057.summary: Add a headers column to http/http2/http3 --csv: emit the observed response headers (the diagnostic-relevant set the human report curates: server, via, cf-ray, cache-control, set-cookie, ...) as Name: value pairs joined by '; ', RFC-4180 quoted per the shared csv_field helper. Renderer-only, no public API change. Pinned by the http --csv fixture test asserting the fixture's server: ip-tools-fixture response header appears in the row.

DEC-056.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface observed HTTP response headers across output formats. The headers are captured and curated in the http/http2/http3 human report and carried in --json, but dropped by the single-shot --csv exporter -- leaving the spreadsheet fleet sweep blind to server identity / CDN hops / caching markers that an operator needs to compare many endpoints at once. Same format-parity pattern the loop closed for TTL (DEC-055) and the probe status feature (DEC-052).
DEC-056.alternatives_rejected: leaving the http CSV without a headers column (the exporters would disagree on what the probes observe); a separate non-default flag just for headers (one column belongs in the existing exporter); dumping all 24 bounded headers into the cell (the curated set matches the human view and keeps rows tight).

CHG-050.summary: Added a headers column to http/http2/http3 --csv: render_http_csv now emits host,...,not_after_utc,headers,failure, populating the field from the observed response headers (the curated diagnostic-relevant set) as 'Name: value' pairs joined by '; ' via a shared curated_headers_csv helper, so a spreadsheet fleet sweep retains the server/edge/caching evidence.

ISS-050.summary: The diagnose command's human report and --json carry each verdict's evidence + possible_causes, but the diagnose --csv exporter (render_csv) emits only host,severity,category,confidence,summary -- a spreadsheet fleet sweep loses the reasoning behind each verdict (the observations that support it and the mundane alternatives that remain). Same format-parity gap the loop closed for TTL (DEC-055), http headers (DEC-056) and the probe status.

TASK-058.summary: Add evidence and possible_causes columns to diagnose --csv: emit each Diagnosis's evidence details and possible causes as semicolon-joined cells (RFC-4180 quoted via the shared csv_field), so a spreadsheet fleet sweep keeps the reasoning behind each verdict. Renderer-only, no public API change. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: the diagnose --csv row carries the fixture QUIC verdict's evidence and possible causes.

DEC-057.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface each diagnosis's evidence and possible causes across output formats. A diagnose fleet sweep in a spreadsheet currently gets only a category + summary -- the WHY (the observations that support the verdict and the alternatives that remain) that the human report and --json carry is dropped, so an operator comparing many hosts cannot tell from the CSV what evidence drove a verdict. Same format-parity pattern the loop closed for TTL, http headers and the probe status.
DEC-057.alternatives_rejected: leaving the diagnose CSV without evidence (the exporters would disagree on what a diagnosis conveys); a separate --evidence flag (the columns belong in the existing exporter); splitting evidence into multi-line cells (one cell per diagnosis keeps rows pivotable on host).

CHG-051.summary: Added evidence and possible_causes columns to diagnose --csv: render_csv now emits host,severity,category,confidence,summary,evidence,possible_causes, joining each diagnosis's Evidence.detail entries and possible_causes into semicolon-separated cells via a shared join_semis helper (RFC-4180 quoted), so a spreadsheet fleet sweep keeps the reasoning behind each verdict.

ISS-051.summary: The repeated HTTP probes surface a status distribution (ProbeResult.status_counts, TASK-052/DEC-051), but the diagnostic engine ignores it: interrupt_status_flapping -- a transport-healthy endpoint that flaps between 2xx and non-2xx (degraded backend, A/B/partial deployment, capacity/rate-limit cycling) is invisible because intermittent_rules only fires when transport attempts actually fail. diagnose also never collected an HTTP status repeat (only tcp_repeat), so the signal was unreachable end-to-end.

TASK-059.summary: Flag HTTP status flapping: add an http_status_flapping_rules engine rule that raises an Intermittent (High) diagnosis when a repeat probe has >=2 attempts, a non-empty status_counts, and observes both 2xx and non-2xx classes; and make diagnose's probe phase collect an HTTP/1.1 status repeat alongside the TCP repeat so the signal is reachable end-to-end. No public API change. Pinned by engine unit tests (flap fires on mixed classes; uniform/single stay silent) and a fixture-gated CLI test: diagnose --sni flap.invalid alternates 200/503 and surfaces the verdict.

DEC-058.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): act on the HTTP status distribution instead of just surfacing it. The probe path reports status_counts (TASK-052) but the diagnostic engine never used them -- only transport failures trigger Intermittent -- so a backend flapping 200<->503 on a transport-healthy path went undiagnosed, exactly the instability an operator running a stability repeat cares about. Also wire an HTTP status repeat into diagnose so the rule is reachable through the flagship command, not just a library API.
DEC-058.alternatives_rejected: leaving the status distribution purely informational (it would stay invisible to diagnose for exactly the flapping case it exists to reveal); reusing the transport Intermittent rule (status class is unrelated to transport success/failure); adding the HTTP repeat to every protocol (h1 status repeat is the canonical signal and bounds diagnose's added cost).

CHG-052.summary: Added HTTP status flapping detection: new http_status_flapping_rules engine rule raises an Intermittent (High) diagnosis when a repeat probe has >=2 attempts and observed both 2xx and non-2xx status classes (reading ProbeResult.status_counts); and diagnose's probe phase now runs an HTTP/1.1 status repeat alongside the TCP repeat so the rule is reachable end-to-end. Added a fixture 'flap.invalid' route that alternates 200/503 (separate TCP/QUIC counters).

ISS-052.summary: The repeat probes already compute per-attempt latency percentiles (p50/p95) and jitter in ProbeResult.latency, but the diagnostic engine never uses them: a transport-healthy, status-stable endpoint with a long latency tail (p95 well above p50 -- degraded backend under load, capacity/rate-limit throttling, congested/flapping path) is invisible because intermittent_rules only fires on transport failures and http_status_flapping only on mixed status classes. The flasking performance analog of status flapping (TASK-059) is undiagnosed.

TASK-060.summary: Flag latency instability: add a latency_instability_rules engine rule that raises an Intermittent (High) diagnosis when a repeat probe succeeds (no transport failures) with >=3 attempts and a latency tail where p95 >= 3*p50. It reads the jitter/percentile data the repeat probes already populate (the HTTP status repeat diagnose now runs), so no public API/CLI change. Pinned by engine unit tests (slow tail fires; tight / <3 attempts / transport failures stay silent) and a fixture-gated CLI test: diagnose <addr> --sni slowflap.invalid (fixture alternates fast / ~120ms with stable 200) surfaces the verdict.

DEC-059.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): act on the latency statistics the repeat probes already compute instead of just rendering them. diagnose now collects an HTTP status repeat (TASK-059), so per-attempt latency is present, yet nothing flags a long slow tail -- an endpoint that never fails and keeps a stable status but degrades under load (p95 far above p50) is exactly the performance instability an operator running a stability repeat wants surfaced, and it is invisible to transport and status rules. A scale-free p95/p50 ratio keeps the threshold defensible across endpoints.
DEC-059.alternatives_rejected: leaving the latency distribution purely informational (it would stay invisible for the exact degrading-backend case it exists to reveal); reusing intermittent_rules (that rule keyed on transport failures, unrelated to a slow healthy tail); a fixed absolute-ms threshold (not scale-free -- inappropriate across local vs internet hops); adding a new CLI flag (the data is already collected).

CHG-053.summary: Added latency-instability detection: new latency_instability_rules engine rule raises an Intermittent (High) diagnosis when a repeat probe succeeds with >=3 attempts and p95 >= 3*p50 (a long slow tail on an otherwise transport/status-healthy path). Added a fixture 'slowflap.invalid' route that alternates fast / ~120ms responses with a stable 200 (separate TCP/QUIC counters) and a fixture-gated CLI test proving diagnose surfaces the verdict.

ISS-053.summary: Every HTTP-family probe (http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose) connects over TLS — there is no way to probe a cleartext HTTP endpoint (internal services, captive portals, HTTP-only health checks, plaintext proxies). A TLS probe to such an endpoint fails with a handshake error instead of observing the real HTTP behaviour, so the tool cannot report on the plaintext HTTP surface at all.

TASK-061.summary: Add cleartext HTTP/1.1 probing: refactor the http module's probe body so the HTTP/1.1 request/bounded-body/TTFB logic is shared between the existing TLS path and a new raw-TCP path (no handshake), expose http::probe_plain / probe_plain_output, and add a --plain flag to the http CLI (mutually exclusive with --insecure/--tls-version). Public API change (api-baseline regenerated). Pinned by a library test (probe_plain gets a 200 from a new plaintext fixture listener) and a fixture-gated CLI test: http <addr> --plain renders the cleartext 200 / HTTP/1.1 / server header.

DEC-060.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): add cleartext HTTP support. Every HTTP probe is TLS-only, so a plaintext endpoint (internal service, captive portal, HTTP-only health check, plaintext proxy) cannot be observed — a TLS probe fails with a handshake error instead of reporting the real HTTP behaviour. Scope as a vertical slice on the http command first (matching how --tls-version first landed on tls), sharing the existing request/body/TTFB logic so the observation shape (status/headers/body/TTFB) is identical, just without the embedded TLS row.
DEC-060.alternatives_rejected: leaving the probes TLS-only (plaintext endpoints stay unobservable); a separate --plain on every command at once (too broad for one slice; http first, later extend like --tls-version); reusing --insecure for plaintext (insecure still does a TLS handshake, it only skips validation — a different semantics).

CHG-054.summary: Added cleartext HTTP/1.1 probing: refactored http.rs so the HTTP/1.1 request/bounded-body/TTFB logic is shared between the TLS path and a new raw-TCP (no-handshake) path via a generic drive_http1; added public http::probe_plain / probe_plain_output; added a --plain flag to the http CLI (conflicts with --insecure/--tls-version). Added a plaintext fixture listener + library and fixture-gated CLI tests. Public API change (api-baseline regenerated).

EVID-latency-subms.summary: The latency-instability rule's p50==0 guard wrongly skipped a real slow tail when the fixture's fast responses measured 0 ms (sub-millisecond): sorted [0,0,123] gave p50=0 so the rule bailed even though p95=123 was a genuine flap. Fixed by flooring the scale base at max(p50,1); the slowflap route also became a deterministic fast-fast-slow mod-3 pattern.

ISS-054.summary: The cleartext HTTP milestone (DEC-060, CHG-054) added --plain to the single-shot http command, but the repeat probe path (probe --protocol http) — the natural form for a health/stability sweep against a plaintext endpoint — is still TLS-only, so a plaintext HTTP stability check cannot run end-to-end.

TASK-062.summary: Extend --plain to the repeat probe: add probe::http_repeat_plain (repeats cleartext HTTP/1.1 and aggregates status+latency) and route probe --protocol http --plain through it in the CLI, rejecting --plain for non-http protocols with a clear error. Public API change (api-baseline regenerated). Pinned by a library test (http_repeat_plain aggregates 200x3 against the fixture plain listener) and a fixture-gated CLI test: probe <addr> --protocol http --count 3 --plain reports 100% success / 200x3, and --protocol tls --plain fails.

DEC-061.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): complete the cleartext HTTP surface by extending --plain to the repeat probe. The single-shot http --plain (DEC-060) lets an operator inspect one plaintext endpoint, but a health/stability sweep against an internal HTTP service needs the repeated form (probe --protocol http) to see success rate + latency over time — exactly what the loop's --tls-version did when it first landed on one command then extended to the repeat path. --plain is rejected for non-http protocols (it only defines cleartext HTTP/1.1).
DEC-061.alternatives_rejected: leaving --plain single-shot only (a plaintext stability sweep would still force a TLS failure); allowing --plain on tls/http2/http3 repeats (those have no cleartext form / would silently ignore the flag); a separate --plain-http flag (one flag belongs on the existing --protocol http path).

CHG-055.summary: Added probe::http_repeat_plain (repeats cleartext HTTP/1.1 and aggregates status+latency) and routed probe --protocol http --plain through it in the CLI, rejecting --plain for non-http protocols. Public API change (api-baseline regenerated); added a library test + a fixture-gated CLI test proving the plaintext repeat aggregates 200x3 and --protocol tls --plain fails.

ISS-055.summary: The DNS TTL feature (DEC-054/TASK-055) surfaced the record TTL on single-shot rows (human/JSON/CSV), but the dns --count repeat row still leaves the CSV ttl column empty and omits TTL from the human repeat report and repeated-probe JSON -- aggregate_repeat discards each observation's ttl, so a stability sweep cannot see the caching-relevant TTL on the aggregated rows. Inconsistent with the single-shot TTL surface.

TASK-063.summary: Surface the minimum record TTL on dns --count repeat rows: add a ttl: Option<u32> field to DnsRepeatResult, compute it in aggregate_repeat as the minimum across the successful answers (the caching-relevant bound), render it in the human repeat report (ttl: N s) and the repeat CSV ttl column (which exists but was left empty). Public API change (api-baseline regenerated). Pinned by an aggregation unit test (min TTL across a bucket), the render unit test, and a fixture-gated CLI test: dns host.example --doh <fixture> --count 3 --csv carries ttl=60 on the repeat row.

DEC-062.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): complete the DNS TTL feature across the repeat surface. Single-shot rows carry TTL, but dns --count aggregates away each attempt's TTL, leaving the repeat CSV ttl column empty and omitting it from the repeated-probe human/JSON output -- inconsistent for the same feature. Carry the minimum TTL across the successful answers, which is the caching-relevant bound (a record with a shorter TTL expires sooner) and stays meaningful when aggregating.
DEC-062.alternatives_rejected: leaving repeat rows TTL-less (an inconsistency with the single-shot TTL feature); the maximum or mean TTL across attempts (the minimum is the conservative caching-relevant bound that matters operationally); a per-record multi-value TTL on the aggregated row (the repeat surface is keyed by resolver+record-type, so a single minimum is the right shape).

CHG-056.summary: Added a ttl field to DnsRepeatResult, computed in aggregate_repeat as the minimum TTL across the successful answers; rendered in the human repeat report (ttl: N s) and the repeat CSV ttl column. Public API change (api-baseline regenerated); added an aggregation unit test, the render unit test, and a fixture-gated CLI test proving dns --count 3 --csv carries ttl=60.

ISS-056.summary: The diagnostic engine compares HTTP status consistency across wire protocols (cross-protocol) and across address families (IPv4 vs IPv6), but not across the independently-probed addresses of the same hostname: a CDN/anycast/load-balanced host where one address returns 200 and another returns 403/503 (partial deployment, per-node WAF, draining member, one edge failing) is reported per-address but never diagnosed as a cross-address inconsistency.

TASK-064.summary: Add cross-address HTTP status divergence to http_consistency_rules: group completed HTTP observations by (protocol, address family); when a group has >=2 distinct addresses and both 2xx and non-2xx classes, raise a Low Http (Medium confidence) diagnosis naming the divergent addresses and statuses, complementing the existing cross-protocol and cross-family checks. No public API change. Pinned by engine unit tests: cross-address divergence fires (200 vs 503 on two addresses, same protocol+family); a single address or uniform addresses stay quiet.

DEC-063.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): complete the HTTP consistency surface by comparing across the independently-probed addresses of the same host. The engine already flags cross-protocol and cross-family divergence, but the README's headline multi-address case (CDN/anycast/load balancing/partial filtering -- addresses tested independently) was never diagnosed: one address returning 2xx and another non-2xx is a genuine partial-deployment / per-node / draining-member / edge-failure signal that the per-address rows alone leave silent. Group by (protocol, family) so only genuine same-wire, same-family address pairs diverge, and it can't fold into or double-report the existing cross-family/protocol checks.
DEC-063.alternatives_rejected: leaving multi-address divergence undiagnosed (it is the README's explicit independently-tested case and a real partial-deployment signal); folding addresses together across protocols or families (would double-report the existing cross-protocol/cross-family verdicts and be ambiguous); a separate command or flag (this is an engine rule that belongs in the existing diagnose consistency pass).

CHG-057.summary: Added cross-address HTTP status divergence to http_consistency_rules: completed HTTP observations grouped by (protocol, family); a group with >=2 distinct addresses spanning both 2xx and non-2xx raises a Low Http (Medium confidence) diagnosis naming the divergent addresses and statuses. Added unit tests (fires on 200 vs 503 across two addresses; quiet for single address or uniform addresses).

ISS-057.summary: The dns --csv exporter carries latency/TTL stats but never the actual resolved records (addresses, CNAME, MX, TXT, ...) -- the primary data of a DNS query, which the human report and --json both show. A spreadsheet DNS sweep (e.g. exporting a fleet's A records) cannot see what each host resolved to.

TASK-065.summary: Add a records column to dns --csv (renderer-only): emit the resolved DnsRecord values (Display-joined, RFC-4180 quoted via the shared csv_field helper) on single-shot rows, left empty on --count repeat rows (the aggregation does not retain per-answer records). No public API change. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: the dns --doh single-shot --csv rows carry the resolved 192.0.2.77 / 2001:db8::77 records.

DEC-064.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface the actual resolved DNS records in the CSV export. The dns --csv rows carry timing/TTL but drop the answers themselves -- exactly the values an operator exporting a fleet's A/CNAME/MX/TXT set from a spreadsheet wants, and which human/JSON already show. Add on single-shot rows (the aggregation case --count leaves empty, mirroring how repeat rows cannot retain per-answer values).
DEC-064.alternatives_rejected: leaving records out of CSV (a spreadsheet sweep would still have to re-query to see answers); a separate --csv-records flag (one column belongs in the existing exporter); embedding records on repeat rows too (the aggregation does not retain per-answer records, so they cannot be carried there honestly).

CHG-058.summary: Added a records column to render_dns_csv: single-shot rows now emit the resolved DnsRecord values (Display-joined, RFC-4180 quoted) on top of the existing latency/TTL fields; --count repeat rows leave it empty. Renderer-only, no public API change; added a fixture-gated CLI test proving the DoH single-shot rows carry 192.0.2.77 / 2001:db8::77.

ISS-058.summary: The HTTP-family observations capture a bounded response body snippet (body_snippet -- WAF block page, JS challenge, auth/API error, captive-portal prompt), surfaced in the human report and --json, but the http/http2/http3 --csv exporter drops it: a spreadsheet fleet sweep sees status/headers but not the content that makes a status meaningful.

TASK-066.summary: Add a body_snippet column to http/http2/http3 --csv (renderer-only): emit the bounded response-body text via the shared RFC-4180 csv_field helper (it may span commas/quotes/newlines), on the fleet rows the human/JSON body content already carries. No public API change. Pinned by an http --csv fixture assertion that the row carries the snippet.

DEC-065.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface the HTTP body snippet across output formats. The HTTP --csv fleet rows gained headers (DEC-056) but still dropped the bounded body content -- the WAF block page / auth error / captive-portal prompt that makes a bare status meaningful, and which human + --json already carry. One quoted CSV cell matches the headers/tls-column pattern and keeps a fleet sweep spreadsheet inspectionable.
DEC-065.alternatives_rejected: leaving body content out of the http CSV (a spreadsheet sweep would still have to re-run the probe or read JSON to see what the endpoint answered); a separate --csv-body flag (one column belongs in the existing exporter); writing the full unbounded body into a cell (the column carries the same bounded snippet the observation already stores).

CHG-059.summary: Added a body_snippet column to render_http_csv and the HTTP family header: fleet rows now carry the bounded response-body text (RFC-4180 quoted) alongside the status/headers/TLS columns. Renderer-only, no public API change; extended the http --csv fixture test to assert the snippet is present.

ISS-059.summary: The diagnose command's stability phase hard-codes 3 repeated attempts per address for both the TCP transport repeat and the HTTP status repeat. An operator diagnosing incidental flapping, latency instability or intermittency cannot lengthen the observation window (more attempts make subtler instability visible) or shorten it to bound runtime -- unlike probe --count and dns --count which are configurable.

TASK-067.summary: Add diagnosis --count N (default 3, matching the sample the flapping/latency/intermittent rules were tuned against; 0 rejected) and thread it through diagnose_one's repeat phase for both the TCP transport repeat and the HTTP status repeat. CLI-only, no public API change. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: diagnose <addr> --sni flap.invalid --count 1 suppresses the status-flapping verdict (single attempt cannot observe 200<->503) while --count 5 surfaces it, proving the flag is threaded through the repeat phase.

DEC-066.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): make diagnose's stability observation window configurable. The repeat phase's hard-coded 3 attempts mean the flapping / latency-instability / intermittent rules only ever see a 3-sample window -- too short to expose subtle instability, and not adjustable to bound runtime. Adding diagnosis --count (parallel to probe --count / dns --count) lets an operator lengthen or shorten the sample; default 3 keeps the exact behavior the rules were validated with and existing fixture tests depend on.
DEC-066.alternatives_rejected: leaving the stability phase at a fixed 3 (operators could not trade observation window against runtime for subtler instability); reusing probe's count default of 10 (diagnose's rules were tuned to a 3-sample window, so defaulting differently would silently change existing diagnoses); adding a separate --stability-count (that count is exactly what --count means on the sibling commands, one flag is enough).

CHG-060.summary: Added diagnose --count N (default 3, 0 rejected) and threaded it through diagnose_one's repeat phase for both the TCP transport repeat and the HTTP status repeat. CLI-only, no public API change; added a fixture-gated CLI test proving --count 1 suppresses the status-flapping verdict while --count 5 surfaces it.

DEC-067.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): surface the certificate SANs and covers <sni> verdict in the tls/http/http2/http3 --csv exports. The SANs (DEC-024) and the hostname-coverage verdict (DEC-025) already ship in the human report and --json (and the http family human/JSON since DEC-039), but both CSV exporters still drop them: a fleet sweep loaded into a spreadsheet loses the wrong-host/wildcard-mismatch signal exactly where cross-host comparisons happen.
