One sans cell + one covers cell per row matches the tls-columns/headers pattern and needs no new dependency.
DEC-067.alternatives_rejected: not adding covers to the http csv (the cert column exists but the verdict is the actual diagnostic signal); not slowing the repeated probe (renderer-only change, zero probe-path impact)

ISS-060.summary: The tls --csv and the shared http/http2/http3 --csv exporters carry subject/issuer/not_after (and the http family the TLS columns) but drop the certificate SANs and the covers <sni> verdict -- even though the human report and --json both surface them (DEC-024/DEC-025/DEC-039). A spreadsheet fleet sweep does the cross-host wrong-certificate/wildcard-mismatch comparison in a pivot table; without the SANs and verdict columns that evidence is lost at the export boundary.

TASK-068.summary: Append sans and covers columns to the tls/http/http2/http3 --csv exporters (renderer-only): a sans cell with the CertificateSummary.sans joined by ';' and a covers cell with 'yes' when cert_covers_hostname(sni, sans) holds, blank otherwise -- completed rows cover the SNI, mismatched rows (wrong host / wildcard) leave covers blank as the signal. Make cert_covers_hostname pub (binary crate reaches it via ip_tools::report). No public API change (renderer-only + visibility of an existing helper). Pinned by unit tests in src/cli/tls.rs and src/cli/http.rs and the updated http --csv fixture header.

CHG-061.summary: tls/http/http2/http3 --csv carry cert SANs (';'-joined) and the covers verdict ('yes'/blank), mirroring the human report + --json; cert_covers_hostname widened to pub for the CLI exporter

DEC-068.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): add --plain to diagnose so the full pipeline can observe a cleartext HTTP endpoint. The http single-shot (DEC-060) and the repeat probe (DEC-061) already probe plaintext HTTP/1.1, but diagnose always runs TLS probes, so a plaintext internal service / captive portal / HTTP-only health check gets a false 'TLS handshake fails where TCP connects' verdict and the HTTP phase fails at the handshake. diagnose --plain skips the TLS observation phase and runs the HTTP phase + the stability repeat over cleartext HTTP/1.1 -- the endpoint is then observed truthfully end-to-end.
DEC-068.alternatives_rejected: not adding --plain to http2/http3 in diagnose (they are TLS-only protocols; cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c) would be a separate, larger feature and is out of scope); not silently skipping TLS when the target is a plain listener (an explicit opt-in flag keeps the TLS evidence for HTTPS-only targets)

ISS-061.summary: diagnose always runs TLS probes for its HTTP evidence and stability repeat, so against a plaintext HTTP endpoint (internal service, captive portal, HTTP-only health check -- exactly the endpoints http --plain and probe --protocol http --plain already probe) it reports a false 'TLS handshake fails where TCP connects' verdict and the HTTP phase never observes the endpoint truthfully. The full diagnostic pipeline is the last cleartext surface that lacks --plain.

TASK-069.summary: Add --plain to diagnose: accept the flag (mutually exclusive with --insecure/--tls-version, reusing plain_arg), thread it into diagnose_one, and when set skip the TLS observation phase (empty tls observations) while running the HTTP phase via probe_plain_output and the stability repeat via probe::http_repeat_plain -- so a plaintext endpoint is observed end-to-end over cleartext HTTP/1.1 without a false TLS-failure verdict. CLI + pipeline change, no new public API (reuses existing plain entry points). Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: diagnose <fixture-plain-addr> --plain exits 0, renders HTTP ok, and carries no TLS failure verdict.

CHG-062.summary: diagnose --plain: skip the TLS phase and probe the HTTP phase + stability repeat over cleartext HTTP/1.1 (probe_plain_output, http_repeat_plain) so a plaintext endpoint is observed truthfully

DEC-069.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-23): aggregate TTFB in the repeated HTTP probes. The single-shot http/http2/http3 probes already capture ttfb_ms -- the time from request to response headers, the server-response-latency signal -- but the stability repeats (probe --protocol http/http2/http3 --count, the diagnose stability phase) aggregate only total latency, so a repeat sweep cannot tell a slow-to-respond server from a slow body transfer. Surfacing a TTFB LatencySummary (min/p50/p95/max) per HTTP ProbeResult gives HTTP health/stability sweeps the server-response dimension the single-shot report already shows. Public API change (ProbeResult gains a ttfb field; api-baseline regenerated), no new dependency. Pinned by an aggregation unit test + the render/CSV unit tests and a fixture-gated CLI test.
DEC-069.alternatives_rejected: not wiring a new diagnosis rule off TTFB in the same slice (the surface first, diagnose later pattern that TTL/status used); not adding TTFB to the transport repeats (tcp/tls have no such signal -- the field stays empty)

ISS-062.summary: The http/http2/http3 repeat probes (probe --protocol http|http2|http3 --count, and diagnose's stability phase) aggregate success rate, total latency percentiles and status distribution but drop time-to-first-byte -- the server-response-latency signal the single-shot probes already capture (HttpObservation.ttfb_ms). A stability sweep therefore cannot tell a slow-to-respond server from a slow body transfer, which is exactly the distinction an HTTP health sweep needs.

TASK-070.summary: Aggregate TTFB in the repeat HTTP probes: extend the shared repeat_impl tuple to carry an optional per-attempt ttfb_ms, collect it (successful or not) into a TTFB LatencyStats alongside total latency, add a ttfb: LatencySummary field to ProbeResult (empty for tcp/tls transport repeats via the existing summarize), and render it in the human probe report (ttfb: min/p50/p95/max rows), --json (automatic via Serialize), and probe --csv (ttfb_p50/ttfb_p95 columns). reuses existing entry points; no change on failed-attempt-only repeats. Public API change (api-baseline regenerated). Pinned by an aggregation unit test (mixed ttfb values summarize into the field) + render/CSV unit tests + a fixture-gated CLI test.

CHG-063.summary: ProbeResult.ttfb LatencySummary aggregated from each completed HTTP repeat response; human ttfb block, --json field, probe --csv ttfb_* columns; api-baseline regenerated (also records the cert_covers_hostname visibility)

DEC-070.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-24): address-family scope for diagnose (--ipv4/--ipv6). Every per-address probe command (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe) can scope a run to one address family, but diagnose cannot: on a dual-stack host where one family is known-broken the pipeline probes both and emits AddressFamily/interference noise, and an operator testing one family cannot focus the diagnosis. Completing parity (cf. DEC-066, DEC-050, DEC-048) lets --ipv4/--ipv6 scope the whole pipeline (DNS evidence still both-families, probed addresses filtered), and the engine's cross-family rules naturally stay silent because only one family's observations are present.
DEC-070.alternatives_rejected: deferred: an engine-level family-scope field on DiagnosticInput (unneeded — scoping the observations already silences the cross-family rules, verified by a new engine unit test); route --probes-per-hop repeat stats (route has --count-like knobs already); --output-body on repeat probes (rejected by DEC-032); redirect following (rejected by DEC-003)

ISS-063.summary: The diagnose command (the full probe pipeline) is the only probe-family command without --ipv4/--ipv6 address-family scope: tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe all restrict a run to one family, so a dual-stack diagnosis on a host where one family is known-broken probes both families and emits the AddressFamily asymmetry verdict plus per-family noise, and an operator testing one family in isolation cannot focus the diagnosis on it.

TASK-071.summary: Scope the diagnose pipeline to one address family via --ipv4/--ipv6 (parity with every other probe command): add the flags to the diagnose subcommand, thread the family through run_diagnose into diagnose_one, and filter the resolved address pool to the chosen family before the reverse-DNS and destination stages. DNS observations keep both families so resolver evidence is unchanged; an IP-literal of the wrong family resolves to no probeable address (diagnose fails cleanly, matching the no-address path). The engine needs no new input field: with only one family observations present, family_rules and the cross-family HTTP-divergence rule naturally stay silent -- pin that with an engine unit test. Fixture-gated CLI: diagnose <v4-literal> --plain --ipv4 probes the fixture and reports 200 with no AddressFamily verdict; --ipv6 fails cleanly.

CHG-064.summary: Add --ipv4/--ipv6 to diagnose: FamilyScope enum threaded through run_diagnose into diagnose_one filters the resolved address pool (DNS evidence unscoped), an IP-literal of the wrong family fails cleanly, and the engine's cross-family rules stay silent on single-family input. CLI-only, no public API change. Pinned by an engine unit test (single-family input never raises AddressFamily; within-family partial connectivity still fires) and a fixture-gated CLI test (--ipv4 probes the fixture's cleartext 200 with no AddressFamily verdict; --ipv6 fails as no address; --ipv4 --ipv6 is a parse error).

DEC-071.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-24): repeated traceroute with path-stability visibility (route --count N). The route command is the only probe family without a repeat view: it traces once and reports a single rtt_ms per hop, so an operator cannot see whether the path changes over time (flapping next-hops, load-balanced routers, BGP/MPLS churn) or how stable each hop's latency is -- the layer analogue of probe --count / dns --count / the diagnose stability phase. --count N repeats the trace N times and aggregates per hop: distinct router addresses observed, answer rate, min/p50/max latency, and a path_changed flag when more than one router answered a hop. count=1 (default) stays the current single-trace behavior/CSV exactly. Reuses the existing LatencyStats/LatencySummary accumulator (no new latency code). Public API change (new route::RouteHopStats + route::RouteRepeat + route::traceroute_repeat; api-baseline regenerated). Pinned by lib unit tests (stable path: identical runs aggregate, path_changed false, latency summarizes; divergent path: two routers at a hop set path_changed and list both addrs; lost hops counted) + report/cli render + csv unit tests.
DEC-071.alternatives_rejected: deferred: splitting the feature across rounds (surface-repeat now, path-change detection later -- a first slice without path-change would be a thin 're-run N times' and the detection is cheap once aggregating addrs); per-hop jitter/distribution percentiles beyond min/p50/max in the human report (LatencySummary carries them, the CSV keeps min/med/max); --concurrency across route runs (raw-socket trace is sequential by nature); output-body on repeat probes (rejected by DEC-032).

ISS-064.summary: The route (traceroute) command traces once and reports a single rtt_ms per hop, so it cannot show whether the path changes over time -- flapping next-hops, load-balanced routers, BGP/MPLS churn -- or how stable each hop latency is: the one probe family without a repeat view (probe --count, dns --count and the diagnose stability phase all aggregate).

TASK-072.summary: Deliver route --count N (default 1 = today): a lib traceroute_repeat(target, cfg, count) that reruns traceroute N times and aggregates per-hop RouteHopStats (distinct addrs, answered/runs, min/p50/max latency via LatencySummary, path_changed when >1 distinct router) into a RouteRepeat; route --count on the CLI (route_count_arg default 1) with new human (Traceroute (N runs) + per-hop addr(s)/N answered/min/p50/max + path changed marker), json (RouteRepeat) and csv (ttl,hostname,addr,rtt_min_ms,rtt_med_ms,rtt_max_ms,answered,runs,path_changed) rendering; reverse-hostname best-effort for the reported addr. Public API change, api-baseline regenerate. Pinned by lib unit tests (stable/divergent/lost aggregation) and report + cli csv unit tests.

CHG-065.summary: Add route --count N: route::traceroute_repeat + aggregate_runs fold N traces into per-hop RouteHopStats (answered, distinct addrs, min/p50/max via LatencySummary, path_changed when >1 router), a RouteRepeat; route_count_arg (default 1) on the route subcommand; report::render_route_repeat human + repeat --csv renderer; --strict counts fully-lost hops. count=1 keeps single-trace behavior/CSV exactly. Public API change (api-baseline regenerated, 25 lines additive). Pinned by 4 lib aggregation unit tests + report render + cli csv render unit tests.

DEC-072.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-24, operator-directed): beautify/polish the human output and UX (goal: 优化美化输出, 打磨交互性, 使用性, 实用性). Deliver a TTY-aware presentation pass: colored PASS/FAIL, HTTP status classes, cert-expiry hints, route lost/path-changed markers and diagnosis severity badges (green/red/yellow/cyan), gated on stdout being a TTY with a --no-color CLI escape and NO_COLOR env honour (https://no-color.org). Non-TTY / --no-color output stays byte-identical to today so piping, golden tests and CSV/JSON formats are untouched. Surface is a clean vertical slice one user (interactive terminal user) can see and verify in one sentence; feature-evolution mode already active (prior sessions).
DEC-072.alternatives_rejected: (1) Add a colorscheme crate (e.g. owo-colors/colored): rejected — 9 small ANSI helpers are trivial and zero-dependency, keeping the crate lean; (2) Color unconditionally like many CLIs: rejected — breaks piping/grepping and golden-test byte-stability; (3) A full interactive TUI/spinner/REPL: rejected — out of scope for a probe tool whose output is meant to be greppable and scriptable; (4) --color always/never/auto tri-state: rejected for now — --no-color + NO_COLOR + TTY gate covers every real need with the smallest surface.

ISS-065.desc: Human terminal output is monochrome: PASS/FAIL, HTTP status classes, cert-expiry hints, lost/path-changed route markers and diagnosis severity badges carry no visual weight, so a quick terminal scan cannot tell healthy from broken at a glance.

TASK-073.desc: TTY-aware styled human output: thread a Style (color gate) through report::render_* and colorize PASS/FAIL, status classes, expiry, route markers, severity badges; --no-color flag + NO_COLOR env + TTY auto-detect; non-TTY byte-identical.

CHG-066.desc: TTY-aware colored human output: report::render_* take a Style; green/red/yellow/cyan status+severity verdicts gated on TTY with --no-color + NO_COLOR; non-TTY/JSON/CSV byte-identical; style::Style::auto pure-gate truth-tabled; api-baseline regenerated; coverage 93.4%.

ISS-066.desc: diagnose human output has no one-line bottom line: a fleet scan must read every evidence row to answer 'did anything turn up?'; a scan should get one colored verdict line when an anomaly exists.

TASK-074.desc: diagnose verdict trailer: render_diagnoses appends 'Anomalies: N (HIGH: a, MEDIUM: b)' colored red/yellow only when a non-Healthy diagnosis exists; healthy runs stay byte-identical.

CHG-067.desc: diagnose ends with a one-line anomaly verdict trailer (colored red/yellow, absent on healthy runs); renderer-only, no API change; report unit tests pin aggregation + colors.

ISS-067.desc: A multi-target sweep prints nothing until the whole run finishes, so an interactive fleet sweep looks frozen; users need a live per-host progress indication on stderr that disappears when piped.

TASK-075.desc: stderr progress counter for multi-target sweeps: TTY-gated (like the color affordance), \r redraw per completed host, N/N complete tail; never for single targets; stdout untouched.

CHG-068.desc: live per-host progress counter wired into run_probe_flow / dns sweep / run_diagnose (Arc<Progress> + cloned handles); pure gate truth-tabled and silent path pinned; CLI-only.

DEC-073.rationale: Milestone closure for the operator-directed UX/beautification goal (DEC-072). Delivered and verified three net-increment vertical slices to main: (1) TTY-aware colored human output with --no-color/NO_COLOR escapes and byte-identical non-TTY text (CHG-066), (2) a colored 'Anomalies: N (HIGH: a, MEDIUM: b)' verdict trailer on diagnose, absent on healthy runs (CHG-067), (3) a stderr TTY-gated per-host progress counter for multi-target sweeps (CHG-068). All gates green at 6 commits: 258 unit+integration tests + 8 doc, clippy -D warnings -W pedantic -W nursery clean, fmt clean, doc -D warnings clean, api-baseline matches, coverage 93.4%, RIL graph consistent.
DEC-073.alternatives_rejected: Deferred with rationale to avoid patch-stacking (value-gate §11.2): human-readable latency/byte units ('1234 ms' -> '1.23 s', 'bytes' -> 'KiB') is internal text polish below the gate; get/list prettification is marginal; error-channel (stderr) coloring risks scripted stderr parsing for near-zero gain. Re-activate any of these only if a real user scenario makes them executable-value problems. The color pass itself targeted repeated candidate 'full --color always/never/auto tri-state' and 'an external colorscheme crate' and was rejected in DEC-072 (--no-color + NO_COLOR + TTY gate covers the need at zero dependencies).

DEC-074.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-24, operator-directed "start a new milestone"): user-asserted response expectations. The HTTP-family single-shot probes (http/http2/http3) report the actual status and bounded body snippet, but the process exit code only reflects transport completion (--strict) and resolution — an operator's "is my deploy healthy / did the endpoint answer the way I asserted" check still needs a shell pipe to grep. Add --expect-status SPEC (exact 200 or class 2xx) and --expect-contains NEEDLE (substring of the bounded body snippet) on http/http2/http3: every per-address observation must satisfy the assertions (a probe that failed to complete can never match — no response to assert on), otherwise the run exits non-zero with "expectation violated: <dest> .." lines on stderr. A single-process, CI-friendly verdict independent of --strict (--strict gates transport completion; --expect gates response shape; they compose). CLI-only (binary-internal cli module, not re-exported in the lib public API): no public API change, no api-baseline churn, default human/JSON/CSV output byte-identical; the observations already carry status + body_snippet, so a JSON consumer can assert the same facts itself.
DEC-074.alternatives_rejected: (1) Extending the probe --protocol http|http2|http3 repeat form (it aggregates N attempts into one ProbeResult with no per-attempt body; a "all attempts matched the status distribution" semantic is muddier — a natural follow-on slice, not this one); (2) diagnose --expect (its job is the evidence-rule engine producing its own verdicts, not user assertions layered on top); (3) a public-API/JSON schema change carrying expectation results per observation (observations already expose status + body_snippet; JSON consumers can assert themselves; keeping this CLI-run-level avoids api-baseline churn and keeps the data format stable); (4) --expect on tcp/tls (no HTTP status class or body to assert against); (5) comma-list of accepted statuses (a single exact-or-class spec keeps parsing honest; a set-of-codes form can extend later); (6) --follow redirects — already rejected thrice (DEC-003/DEC-041/DEC-070), unchanged here.

ISS-068.desc: A user running an HTTP-family probe (http/http2/http3) sees the actual status and bounded body snippet in the report, but the process exit code only ever reflects transport completion (--strict) and resolution. An operator's "is the deploy healthy / did the endpoint answer the way I asserted" check therefore still needs a shell pipe to grep, so there is no single-process, CI-friendly verdict for "the endpoint answered the way I asserted" — the missing link between measuring an HTTP response and gating on its shape.

TASK-076.desc: Add user-asserted response expectations to the HTTP-family single-shot probes: --expect-status SPEC (exact "200" or class "2xx") and --expect-contains NEEDLE (substring of the bounded body snippet) on http/http2/http3. Every per-address observation must satisfy the assertions (a probe that failed to complete can never match, since there is no response to assert on); the run exits non-zero with "expectation violated: <dest> ..." lines on stderr when any observation violates, independent of --strict. DEC-075.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-24, operator-directed "start a new milestone"): extend the user-asserted expectation gate from the single-shot response (DEC-074) to the repeated-probe stability dimension. The single-shot --expect-status/--expect-contains gates one response's shape, but the exit code of `probe` still only reflects completion: it measures reliability (success_rate, latency distribution, HTTP status distribution over --count attempts) yet cannot gate on it, so an operator's "is this endpoint reliably healthy over time" CI check still needs to parse the report. Add the same assertion hook to `probe`, evaluated per resolved address on the aggregated ProbeResult: (a) --expect-status SPEC (exact `200` or class `2xx`, reusing StatusSpec/parse_status_spec): every observed status in the per-address status distribution must be in the accepted set; an address whose attempts never completed has no response to assert on and violates. (b) --expect-rate RATE (fraction like 0.97 / 1, or percent like 97%%; 0 excluded as vacuous): the per-address aggregate success_rate must meet the threshold. Exit-code semantics mirror DEC-074: the asserted gate is a verdict on the whole run, independent of --strict, naming each violating destination on stderr ("expectation violated: <addr> ...") with the report on stdout untouched. CLI-only (ExpectCheck is cli-internal): no public API change, no api-baseline churn, default/JSON/CSV output byte-identical. Input guard: --expect-status with --protocol tcp|tls errors (no HTTP status exists to assert). This is the DEC-074-deferred "natural follow-on slice", now clean because ProbeResult aggregates status_counts (since the TTFB milestone) and success_rate.
DEC-075.alternatives_rejected: (1) --expect-p95 <ms> latency bound on probe: a performance-SLO plane (p50/p95 budget) distinct from this availability/shape gate; keeping the assertion grammar single-plane (did it answer, with the accepted status, reliably) and deferring latency budgets to a later slice. (2) --expect-status comma-list on the single-shot family (DEC-074 scope-out #5): an expressiveness extension of a shipped feature at the "missing an option" level, and the repeat-form status-set semantics already subsumes its value; deferred. (3) diagnose --expect (DEC-074 scope-out #2): diagnose's job is its own evidence-rule engine producing verdicts; layering user assertions on the orchestrator muddies that separation (a diagnose verdict ALREADY carries its own pass/fail via the anomaly trailer); rejected. (4) --expect-contains on probe (DEC-074 scope-out #1): the aggregated ProbeResult legitimately has no single body to assert on (only a status distribution); unchanged, rejected. (5) TCP/TLS single-shot --expect-status (DEC-074 scope-out #4): no HTTP status to assert against; --expect-rate now naturally covers the transport side of the repeat; rejected.

TASK-078.desc: Add a user-asserted reliability gate to the repeated probe: --expect-status SPEC and --expect-rate RATE on the `probe` subcommand, evaluated per resolved address against the aggregated ProbeResult (success_rate + status_counts). --expect-status reuses StatusSpec/parse_status_spec (exact `200` or class `2xx`): every observed status in the per-address distribution must be in the accepted set; empty distribution (no completed attempt) is itself a violation. --expect-rate parses a fraction (0.97, 1) or percent (97%%): the aggregate success_rate must be >= RATE; 0 rejected as vacuous. Both gate the run exit code independent of --strict, naming each violating destination on stderr ("expectation violated: <addr> ..."); report on stdout untouched. Guards: --expect-status errors when --protocol tcp|tls. CLI-only (ExpectCheck is cli-internal; no public API change; default/JSON/CSV output byte-identical).
